subject: MSA + Order Form: COI timing & entitlement escalation
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@procura.io>
To: david.kim@redwoodinference.com
Cc: contracts_ops@procura.io
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline + insurance schedule (Procura)

Hi David —

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Legal attached a marked copy with two items blocking signature on our side: insurance minimums and timing for the certificate of insurance (COI). Highlights from our redline (see attached):

- General Liability: 2M per occurrence / 4M aggregate.
- Professional Liability (E&O): 2M aggregate.
- Requirement to list Procura, Inc. as Additional Insured on the GL policy via endorsement (ISO CG 20 10 or equivalent).
- COI to be delivered and cleared prior to the effective date of the first SOW/order.

We can be flexible on the form of the endorsement but we cannot proceed without the additional insured language and the COI in hand. Can you confirm Redwood's ability to produce the COI and endorsement language, and whether you have any standard carrier contact we should expect receipts from?

Attaching our redline and a sample COI for reference. If you prefer, we can accept an escrow/holdback arrangement for the first 30 days, but legal prefers to avoid that if COI can be produced up front.

Thanks —
Susan
Contracts Manager
Procura, Inc.

Susan —

Appreciate the quick redline. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Mina (procurement) to confirm. Two quick notes from my side:

1) Redwood typically provides COIs naming the counterparty as Additional Insured by endorsement for customers with enterprise order forms.
2) Coverage minimums are often negotiable by product and region — for hosted API we usually accept 1M/2M GL for lower-risk, but larger customers or specific procurement teams ask for 2M/4M.

Kimberly — can you confirm our preferred fallback language and whether we can accept Procura's ask as-is or suggest a 1.5M compromise? Mina — if COI can be issued within 3 business days of countersignature, will Procura accept that timing?

Thanks,
David
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com
To: david.kim@redwoodinference.com, mina_haddad@redwoodinference.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2026 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline + insurance schedule (Procura)

Team —

Reviewed Procura's redline. Quick legal assessment:

- Additional Insured: acceptable in principle. We need the endorsement to be limited to liability arising from Redwood's performance under the agreement (CG 20 10 narrow form). We should avoid unlimited blanket endorsements.
- Limits: for enterprise deals we have precedent accepting 1M/2M GL and 1M E&O. However, if Procura is insistent, we can agree to 2M/4M GL + 2M E&O for this particular SOW if they provide procurement justification (data sensitivity / regulated workload) or if this is a platform-wide integration.
- Timing: we prefer COI at or immediately after countersignature. Requiring COI before signature is a procurement ask but not typical; if Procura insists on pre-signature COI, procurement should escalate to confirm their approval matrix.

Proposed position to offer Procura: Accept 1M/2M GL + 1M E&O and provide an Additional Insured endorsement limited to Redwood-related operations; require COI within 3 business days post-execution. If Procura cannot accept, escalate to execs to approve the higher limits.

Aditya, please prepare a one-paragraph justification we can present to Procura if they push for 2M limits (we should focus on risk posture and cost impact).

Kimberly
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_insurance_guidance_v1.pdf)

Susan —

Procurement here. Thanks for the redline. A few logistics notes:

- Our broker confirms Redwood's insurer can issue a COI and the Additional Insured endorsement. Typical turnaround is 2–4 business days after countersignature.
- To avoid blocking your procurement flow, would Procura accept the following operational compromise: countersign the MSA and Order Form, Redwood to deliver COI + endorsement within 72 hours, and Procura reserves the right to pause provisioning if COI is not received. This avoids holding the contract in procurement while giving you assurance.
- If Procura absolutely requires a carrier-sent COI prior to countersignature, please confirm the specific holder (email) we should use so we can coordinate with our broker now.

If you want, we can run a short phone call with legal and procurement to finalize. Available Wed 10–11am PT.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
